sketches.notes: Base plate 60 mm (X) x 40 mm (Y) centered on origin. Spans X[-30,30], Y[-20,20]. Extruded upward in +Z to form the base plate Z[0,6].

Vertical wall profile on XZ plane placed at world Y=+20 (offset -20.0). Local sketch x -> world X, local sketch y -> world Z. Explicit quad spans local x[-30,30], local y[0,40] => world X[-30,30], Z[0,40]. Sketch deliberately starts at Z=0 (extends THROUGH the base plate) so the extruded wall overlaps the base volume and can be unioned. Extrude 6 mm along +normal (-Y) gives wall Y[14,20].

steps.label: Extrude base plate
steps.notes: Base plate solid, Z from 0 to 6, X[-30,30], Y[-20,20]. This is the reference body for the L-bracket.

steps.label: Extrude vertical wall
steps.notes: Vertical wall solid. Sketch plane at world Y=+20, extruded 6 mm along -Y => wall occupies Y[14,20], X[-30,30], Z[0,40]. Wall bottom face is at Z=0 so it fully overlaps the base plate (Z=0..6) for a clean union.

steps.label: Union wall to base plate
steps.notes: Fuse base plate and vertical wall into a single L-shaped solid. Resulting solid has one inner concave edge at the intersection of the wall inner face (Y=14) and the base top face (Z=6), running along world X.

steps.label: Fillet inner concave corner (wall/base)
steps.notes: Apply R=FILLET_RADIUS=2.0 mm ONLY to the single inner concave edge where the vertical wall inner face (Y=14) meets the base plate top face (Z=6); this edge is horizontal (parallel to XY) and runs along world X from x=-30 to x=+30. Refine the edge selection to this concave (interior) edge only, e.g. by keeping only the horizontal edge whose midpoint is at (0, 14, 6). Do NOT fillet outer convex edges (base bottom perimeter at Z=0, base outer top perimeter at Z=6, wall top edge at Z=40) or vertical edges. This concave fillet adds material into the corner and therefore does not change the overall bounding box (X=60, Y=40, Z=40), keeps the part a single connected solid, and preserves watertightness. FILLET IS THE LAST STEP — applied after all additive and boolean operations.
